scope.invariant: An injected Store serializes native context/identity/epoch/expiry checks; injected time must be sampled after transaction admission, and selected data is returned only after provenance/history successfully commits.
scope.selectedChain: Runtime::recover -> host_session/create_session -> host_context -> check_context/check_capability and selected read -> Store::transaction -> bound_context/check_session -> policy/combination -> result; injected InstallFiles contract and host_package_session proof handoff inspected without expanding package recovery.
allowedPaths: crates/am-plugin-runtime public ports, authority and selected read helpers
expansionReasons: Selected read helpers show how the same public Store/Clock contract is safely applied and how history commits before data return.

The guard implementation samples time before Store admission; one direct executor neighbor establishes concrete bootstrap/final-result and broker-capability uses. SQLite and executor lifecycle internals remain outside this batch.
exclusions: InstallFiles filesystem implementation, install/rollback/recovery and anonymous transport
App/browser/emulator inspection, root final acceptance, commit and push

declaredStatus.claim: Runtime uses only protocol/policy/serde/serde_json with injected Store/Clock/Ids/InstallFiles; every operation rechecks actual native identity, epoch and lifetime.
declaredStatus.assessment: Dependency and port ownership conform; two context/capability guard paths violate the lifetime-check ordering under Store contention.

checks.question: Does runtime own native orchestration without concrete IO, DB or global-clock dependencies?
checks.detail: Only protocol/policy/serialization dependencies are declared; complete closure passes the existing metadata boundary check. No concrete filesystem/network/database/framework/global-clock implementation is imported by runtime.

checks.question: Are authority inputs and durability/time/ID/file ports explicit and native-only?
checks.detail: Caller has no Deserialize; runtime is generic over Store/Clock/Ids and accepts InstallFiles explicitly. verify_pair returns owned verified bytes; session proof binds identity and epoch. Actual native caller construction, filesystem durability and package-recovery ordering are not accepted here.

checks.question: Do context and capability checks evaluate expiry against transaction-admission time?
checks.detail: Both guards capture now_ms before Store::transaction. Six independent grant/session/context deadline probes return Ok after time advances to expiry at Store admission; each is valid before waiting and must return Expired after admission.

checks.question: Do selected-data reads and recovery stop on failed durable commits without leaking data or partial epoch changes?
checks.detail: Memory-Store failure injection proves read returns Storage and retains no partial delivery/history; read samples the clock inside admission. Recovery returns no runtime on commit failure, and a second-install epoch overflow rolls back the first increment. These are injected-Store proofs, not SQLite durability evidence.

checks.question: Are actual session/caller identities, epoch and selected object versions checked against the current ledger?
checks.detail: Bound context checks real channel/document/account; session checks full install identity, enabled flag and epoch. Selected read checks object versions before projection. Existing replacement, restart, context closure, forged caller and corruption regressions pass. The separate expiry-order defect remains open.

testSummary.expiryFailureMatrix: 2 guard methods x 3 independent expiration bounds
testSummary.expectedFailure: The failing public-API probes demonstrate B14-R01 and are not suppressed.

findings.title: Sample authorization time after entering the Store transaction
findings.trigger: Call check_context or check_capability while now < the grant/session/context expiry, then let Store acquisition wait until now >= that expiry before invoking the transaction closure.
findings.observed: All six guard/expiry combinations return Ok(()) instead of Err(Expired). Positive controls succeed before the wait; already-expired controls and read with transaction-local time deny correctly.
findings.effect: Expired context/capability checks can authorize after Store contention. Direct executor callers use check_context before guest bootstrap/final-output delivery and check_capability before broker operations.
findings.limit: Reproduced against the unchanged runtime with a deterministic injected Store/Clock, not a live native SQLite queue. Native epoch/revocation checks still use current ledger state; this finding does not establish unauthorized persisted writes. No executor exploit or live runtime acceptance is claimed.
findings.suggestedAction: Borrow self.clock before transaction, then call clock.now_ms() inside each transaction closure before bound_context, matching read/create_session/host_context. Add permanent delayed-admission regressions for both methods and all expiry sources; rerun runtime and direct executor tests.

probeEvidence.implementation: Audit-only module includes existing test-owned fixtures, then wraps Memory::transaction to advance the injected clock immediately after admission. A native-only seeded PackageRecord supplies the exact crypto.sha256 grant for capability controls; no production seed was added.
probeEvidence.retention: Ignored local source, compile/build artifacts and logs; permanent product tests remain unchanged.
probeEvidence.recoveredHarnessIssues: Initial standalone compilation assumed a nonexistent top-level serde_json rlib; use of the Cargo-emitted artifact fixed compilation. Final audit_ports:: filter runs only the 11 local tests; six runtime failures remain. Initial compile and first run are retained separately.

Named commit/revoke atomic values/provenance/receipts/version/idempotency and real multi-connection competition remain B14-named-commit-revoke.
InstallFiles behavior beyond its public owned-byte/proof handoff, verified install/rollback/recovery and precise target admission are not accepted.
Direct executor excerpts establish call sites only; complete production IPC/caller/consent and executor lifecycle remain separate.
Production artifacts, live app/browser checks and repository-wide final gates were not run for this audit without implementation changes.

Native SQLite/permit/commit race and package-recovery tests
